successors.name: Koch Hajo
successors.text: Raghudev's eastern portion: Goalpara, Kamrup and, bridged, the Barak Valley

ledger.x: 1515: 'Biswa Singha announced himself the king of Kamata bounded on the east by Barnadi River' and on the west by the Karatoya; the infobox gives 1515 as the founding year and the State page gives Kamatapur as capital from 1515.
1562: 'The Barak valley was obtained by Chilarai in 1562' from the Twipra (Tripura) kingdom; he set up a garrison that became the Khaspur state (a Koch dewani).
1581: Raghudev, 'who had accepted the suzerainty of his uncle', rules the eastern portion as a tributary of Nara Narayan.
1587: 'When Nara Narayan died in 1587, Raghudev stopped paying tribute and declared himself independent.'
1693: the capital moves from Kamatapur to Cooch Behar (infobox: 'Kamatapur (1515-1693); Cooch Behar (1693-1950)').
1711: 'The Mughals took Boda, Patgram and eastern Pargana in the year 1711.'
1949: the state 'immediately acceded to and merged with India in 1949'.

wars.name: Koch conquest of the Barak Valley
wars.outcome: Chilarai's expedition took the Barak Valley from Tripura and left a garrison, later the Khaspur state.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Koch Hajo
wars.outcome: Mughal forces, allied with Lakshmi Narayan of Koch Bihar, attacked Parikshit Narayan of Koch Hajo in 1612; Koch Hajo was occupied by the end of that year and Parikshit was sent to Delhi (Koch dynasty page); the Koch Hajo page has the expedition leaving Dhaka…

wars.name: British-Koch war against Bhutan
wars.outcome: A British-Koch coalition captured the capital in 1772; the British negotiated a peace with Bhutan on 25 April 1774 and Cooch Behar became a protectorate of the Company.

certainty.note: The pages give the Karatoya and Barnadi as the limits, the Manas as the line of the 1581 split and no area; the shapes are discs round the Cooch Behar country and the Goalpara and Kamrup plains.
The final area (3,385 km2 in 1901) is known but the boundary is a disc; the Duars, held by Bhutan from the early 17th century and returned to British India in 1865, are not drawn.
